notes.meaning: Obadiah shares a vision given to him by the Lord concerning the neighboring nation of Edom. God sends out a royal messenger among the nations to summon them to rise up and fight against her. Even when human kings start wars, the Lord is the one directing events from above to carry out His justice.

differ.view: Some commentators believe Obadiah wrote during the Babylonian exile, viewing Edom's punishment as connected to the destruction of Jerusalem.
Some commentators place Obadiah much earlier, during an attack on Jerusalem under King Jehoram, making him the earliest writing prophet.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Most modern scholars date the book to the sixth century BC, understanding the prophecy as a response to Edom's role in the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BC.

notes.meaning: God announces that He has decided to humble Edom and make her small among the surrounding nations. Even though Edom held a high opinion of herself, she would become deeply despised. The rise and fall of every nation rests entirely in God's hands.

Edom's people were filled with pride because their homes were carved high up in steep rocky cliffs, such as the fortress city of Petra. They thought their mountain cliffs were so secure that no army could ever reach them. Their proud hearts fooled them into thinking they were beyond any danger.

The Lord answers Edom's boast by warning that no height can hide anyone from His hand. Even if they could soar like eagles and build their nests among the stars, God promises to bring them down. Human defenses cannot protect anyone when God calls them to account.

Night thieves steal only until they have taken enough, and grape pickers always leave a few grapes behind on the vine. But Edom will face complete ruin, with nothing spared. Invaders will thoroughly search every hidden cave and rocky crevice to carry off all of Esau's stored treasures.

Edom's trusted allies and peace partners will turn against her and drive her people to the frontier. The very friends who ate at her table will lay a secret trap to destroy her. Edom was known for its wisdom, yet her leaders will fail to recognize the danger until it is too late.

The Lord promises that when the day of judgment arrives, He will remove the understanding of Edom's wise men. The region was famous throughout the ancient world for its deep knowledge and sound advice. Yet God will cause their counsel to fail so that their best plans cannot save them.

The brave soldiers of the southern district of Teman will lose all their courage and panic in fear. When the strongest fighters fail, the entire country is left completely defenseless against the invaders. Every warrior in the mountains of Esau will be cut down in the battle.

God gives the exact reason for Edom's destruction: its cruel violence against Jacob, its own brother nation. Because the Israelites and Edomites came from the twin brothers Jacob and Esau, Edom should have shown family loyalty instead of hatred. Because of this shameful betrayal, Edom will be cut off forever as a people.

When foreign armies broke into Jerusalem and cast lots to divide its wealth and prisoners, Edom stood across the way and did nothing to help. By watching with approval and taking part in the plunder, Edom acted just like the foreign invaders. Refusing to help a brother in trouble made them partners in the crime.

The Lord rebukes Edom for looking on its brother's suffering with malicious joy. Instead of weeping for Judah in its dark hour, the Edomites cheered, gloated, and spoke proud, mocking words against the victims. God is deeply offended whenever people celebrate the downfall of others.

Edom had no right to march through the broken gates of Jerusalem on the day of its defeat. They should not have stared with pleasure at their brother's suffering or greedily stolen his remaining goods. God took notice of every single thing they looted while the city was defenseless.

The Edomites acted with extreme cruelty by waiting at the crossroads and mountain passes to trap fleeing Judaeans. They killed some of the terrified refugees on the spot and handed over the survivors to the enemy as prisoners. Trapping helpless people who are running for their lives was their worst offense.

The Day of the Lord is near, when God will judge all nations for how they have lived and treated others. What Edom did to Judah will be done back to Edom, and its cruel actions will fall upon its own head. God's justice ensures that oppressors will one day face the very suffering they brought on others.

Just as God's people were made to drink the bitter cup of judgment on His holy mountain, all the hostile nations will now be forced to drink God's wrath. They will swallow it down to the very dregs without any relief. Their destruction will be so total that it will be as if they had never existed at all.

In contrast to the ruined nations, Mount Zion will be an escape and a place of safety for a rescued remnant. The holy mountain will be cleansed from defilement and set apart for God alone. The house of Jacob will return from captivity and reclaim the land God gave them.

The reunited people of Jacob and Joseph will become like a blazing fire, while the house of Esau will be like dry stubble. God will empower His people to burn up and consume their ancient enemy. The Lord Himself has spoken, promising that no survivor will remain to carry on the nation of Edom.

The returning people of God will spread out and occupy the lands of their former enemies. Those living in the southern desert will possess the mountains of Edom, while those in the foothills will take over the Philistine plains. They will also settle the fertile fields of Samaria and expand across the Jordan into Gilead.

Exiles from the northern tribes will return to possess the northern coastlands of Canaan all the way to Zarephath. The captives from Jerusalem scattered in distant places like Sepharad will come back to inhabit the southern cities. God will bring His scattered people home to an enlarged inheritance.

God will raise up deliverers on Mount Zion to govern and bring judgment upon the mountains of Edom. These leaders pointed forward to Christ and the spread of His gospel through His messengers. In the end, all human pride will fall away, and the kingdom will belong fully to the Lord.
